scale.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000000: "üks biljon"; CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000000000: "üks biljard": "biljon" is 10^12, a million millions, so Estonian counts in the long scale.

group_mark.source: CLDR 48 et number symbols: group U+00A0; Wikipedia, "Decimal separator": Estonia writes "1 234 567,89".

decimal_mark.source: CLDR 48 et number symbols: decimal ","; Wikipedia, "Decimal separator": Estonia writes "1 234 567,89".

space_groups.source: Wikipedia, "Decimal separator": Estonia writes "1 234 567,89" with a space between the groups.

scale_noun_agrees.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext): numerals take a "noun in singular nominative for 1 and in singular partitive for others"; so "üks miljon" but "kaks miljonit" (CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000: "üks miljon"; CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2000000: "kaks miljonit").

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2000000: "kaks miljonit": the partitive "miljonit" follows a count; alone it names no number.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 21: "kakskümmend üks": no conjunction joins the parts.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 101: "ükssada üks": no conjunction joins the parts.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1001: "üks tuhat üks": no conjunction joins the parts.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: No joiner stands after the thousands (joiner_between_groups is never): CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1500: "üks tuhat viissada"; CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1020: "üks tuhat kakskümmend".

ordinal_style.source: Estonian ordinals are entries with "ordinal": true; a number whose last word is ordinal is ordinal ("kahekümne viies"). No entry has the role "ordinal".

compound_words.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext), numerals (nominative - genitive - partitive): "üks - ühe - üht (1), kaks - kahe - kaht (2), kolm - kolme - kolme (3), neli - nelja - nelja (4), viis - viie - viit (5), kuus - kuue - kuut (6), seitse - seitsme - seitset (7), kaheksa - kaheksa - kaheksat (8), üheksa - üheksa - uheksat (9), kümme - kümne - kümmet (10), -teist(kümmend) - -teist(kümne) - -teist(kümmet) (11-19), -kümmend - -kümne - -kümmet (20-90), sada - saja - sadat (100), -sada - -saja - -sadat (200-900), - tuhat - - tuhande - - tuhandet, - miljon - - miljoni - - miljonit, - miljard - - miljardi - - miljardit": "-kümmend", "-sada" and "-teist" join their count in one word ("kakskümmend", "kakssada", "kaksteist").

inflection_position.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext): "Adjectival modifiers (including ordinals ...) agree with their heads in case and number"; every part of a numeral takes the case, and in the last four cases the parts before the last stay in the genitive.

dot_ordinal.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_orthography.wikitext): "The period (full stop) is used at the end of sentences, as an ordinal mark".

joiner.source: "ja" (and) joins a half to a number ("kaks ja pool"), as "poolteist" names one and a half; no conjunction joins the parts of a number (CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 21: "kakskümmend üks").

minus.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal renders -5 as "miinus viis".

minus_idioms.source: No Estonian idiom puts "miinus" before a positive number.

article_one.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext): "the function of the indefinite article can be performed by the indefinite pronoun üks, developed from the numeral one"; alone before a noun it is a weak number.

of.source: Estonian has no word that multiplies a scale word.

fraction_of.source: Estonian puts no word between a fraction and a collective.

denominator_particle.source: Estonian has no particle like Portuguese "avos".

class_noun.source: Estonian has no class noun after a collective.

half_unit.source: Estonian puts "pool" before the unit ("pool kilo").

abbreviation.source: No Estonian number word is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: The comma is the Estonian decimal mark (CLDR 48 et), so ",5" is 0.5.

range_cue.source: Estonian puts "vahel" (between) after the numbers, as a postposition with the genitive ("kahe ja viie vahel"); no word before a range opens it.

digit_suffix_mark.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_orthography.wikitext): "Case forms of cardinal and ordinal numerals may be written in the form "figures+case ending" with or without a hyphen: 16s or 16-s"; the ending after the hyphen is no number word.

et.bare.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext): the genitive and the partitive are the bare stem ("genitive ∅ (with vowel)", "partitive -d, -t, ∅"); each stem listed with this class is that form.

et.case.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext), case table (singular): illative "-sse", inessive "-s", elative "-st", allative "-le", adessive "-l", ablative "-lt", translative "-ks", terminative "-ni", essive "-na", abessive "-ta", comitative "-ga", each on the genitive stem; "In the terminative, essive, abessive, and comitative the modifier agrees only in number and remains in the genitive."
